==English==
{{wp}}

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|smal}}, {{m|enm|smale}}, {{m|enm|small}}, {{m|enm|smalle}}, {{m|enm|smel}}, {{m|enm|smæl}}, from {{inh|en|ang|smæl|t=narrow, slim; slender; fine; small; quiet}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*smal}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*smalaz|t=small}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)mal-|t=small; little}}. 
{{col-top|2|cog}}
Cognate with {{cog|sco|smaw|t=small; minor}}, {{cog|yol|smaale}}, {{m|yol|small|t=small}}, {{cog|frr|smaal}}, {{m|frr|smeel}}, {{m|frr|smääl|t=narrow}}, {{cog|stq|smäl|t=narrow}}, {{cog|fy|smel|t=narrow}}, {{cog|gsw|schmaal|t=narrow}}, {{cog|bar|schmoi|t=narrow; slender}}, {{cog|nl|smal|t=narrow; small}}, {{cog|de|schmal|t=narrow; slender}}, {{cog|nds|small|t=narrow; slender, small}}, {{cog|lb|schmuel|t=narrow}}, {{cog|wym|śmoł}}, {{m|wym|šmoł|t=narrow}}, {{cog|yi|שמאָל|t=narrow}}, {{cog|da,nb,nn,sv|smal|t=narrow; slim}}, {{cog|got|𐍃𐌼𐌰𐌻𐌹𐍃𐍄𐍃|t=smallest}}; also {{cog|la|malus|t=bad, distressing, nasty; evil, mischievous, wicked; destructive, hurtful, noxious; abusive, hostile, unkind}}, {{cog|be|малы́|t=small}}, {{cog|bg,mk|мал|t=small; minor}}, {{cog|cs,sk|malý|t=small}}, {{cog|pl|mały|t=small; little; humble; short}}, {{cog|ru|ма́лый|t=small; short}}, {{cog|sh|ма̑л}}, {{m|sh|mȃl|t=small}}, {{cog|uk|мали́й|t=small}}.

===Adjective===
{{en-adj|er}}

# Not [[large]] or [[big]]; [[insignificant]]; [[few]] in [[number]].
#: {{syn|en|little|microscopic|minuscule|minute|tiny|Thesaurus:small}}
#: {{ant|en|big|generous<q:said of an amount of something given>|large|Thesaurus:large}}
#: {{ux|en|A '''small''' serving of ice cream.}}
#: {{ux|en|A '''small''' group.}}
#* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=5|passage=Here, in the transept and choir, where the service was being held, one was conscious every moment of an increasing brightness; colours glowing vividly beneath the circular chandeliers, and the rows of '''small''' lights on the choristers' desks flashed and sparkled in front of the boys' faces, deep linen collars, and red neckbands.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-06-22|volume=407|issue=8841|page=70|magazine=w:The Economist
|titleurl=http://www.economist.com/news/finance-and-economics/21579879-buy-out-firm-really-does-focus-operational-improvements-engineers|title=Engineers of a different kind
|passage=Private-equity nabobs bristle at being dubbed mere financiers. Piling debt onto companies’ balance-sheets is only a '''small''' part of what leveraged buy-outs are about, they insist. Improving the workings of the businesses they take over is just as core to their calling, if not more so. Much of their pleading is public-relations bluster.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20201125211145/https://www.economist.com/finance-and-economics/2013/06/22/engineers-of-a-different-kind}}
#* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Ashley Strickland|title=The reason we’re shooting laser beams between Earth and the moon|url=https://www.cnn.com/2020/08/13/world/nasa-moon-lasers-scn-trnd/index.html|date=2020-08-13|passage=The orbiter has been observing the moon since 2009, and its reflector is a '''smaller''' version of reflector panels placed on the lunar surface during the Apollo 11, 14 and 15 landings on the moon. Soviet lunar robotic landers sent in 1970 and 1973 also carried '''smaller''' reflectors.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20251009212617/https://www.cnn.com/2020/08/13/world/nasa-moon-lasers-scn-trnd/index.html|archivedate=9 October 2025}}
#* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Chris Lau and Nodoka Katsura|title=This is the world’s smallest Rubik’s Cube. And it actually works|url=https://www.cnn.com/2024/10/04/style/japan-worlds-smallest-rubik-cube-intl-hnk/index.html|date=2024-10-04|passage=Guinness World Record confirmed the micro-cube as the world’s '''smallest''' rotating puzzle cube in August.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20251112015844/https://www.cnn.com/2024/10/04/style/japan-worlds-smallest-rubik-cube-intl-hnk/index.html|archivedate=12 November 2025}}
## [[humiliated|Humiliated]] or [[insignificant]].
##: ''The bullies had succeeded in making him feel '''small'''.''
##* {{quote-song|en|year=2015|author=w:Justin Bieber|title=w:Love Yourself
|passage=For all the times that you made me feel '''small''' / I fell in love, now I feel nothing at all}}
## Having a small [[penis]], [[muscles]], or other important body parts, regardless of overall body size.
##: {{syn|en|little|under-endowed}} {{q|of genitals}}
##: {{usex|en|Though over six feet tall, the man was very '''small''' and ashamed to undress.}}
# {{lb|en|figuratively|incomparable}} [[young|Young]], as a [[child]].
#: {{syn|en|little|wee<q:Scottish>|young}}
#: {{ant|en|adult|grown-up|old}}
#: {{ux|en|Remember when the children were '''small'''?}}
# {{lb|en|writing|incomparable}} [[minuscule|Minuscule]] or [[lowercase]], referring to written or printed [[letter]]s.
#: {{syn|en|lowercase|minuscule}}
#: {{ant|en|big|capital|majuscule|uppercase}}
# Evincing little [[worth]] or [[ability]]; not large-[[minded]]; [[paltry]]; [[mean]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1851|author=w:Thomas Carlyle|title=w:The Life of John Sterling
|passage=A true delineation of the '''smallest''' man is capable of interesting the greatest man.}}
# Not prolonged in duration; not extended in time; short.
#: {{ux|en|a '''small''' space of time}}
# {{synonym of|en|little||of an industry or institution(s) therein: operating on a small scale, unlike larger counterparts}}.
#: ''[[small science|'''small''' science]]''
# {{lb|en|archaic}} Slender, gracefully slim.
# {{lb|en|especially|clothing|food|or|drink}} That is small {{gl|the manufactured size}}.
#: {{ux|en|I'll have a '''small''' coffee, thanks.}}

{{en-adv|er}}

# In a small fashion
#: {{ux|en|Don't write very '''small'''!}}

# {{lb|en|obsolete}} To a small extent.
